purpose: How a plating bench designs the whole deposited stack for a specific piece — which strike bonds it, which barrier class blocks diffusion and carries corrosion life, how many microns go to underplate versus gold for the wear class and the claim, how each interface is kept bondable, and which post-plate topcoat class (if any) is added — so the finish survives wear rather than merely looking right on the day it leaves the tank.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

every bath in the stack is a purchased commercial plating product operated per its technical data sheet; the TDS and the shop's own logged runs govern setpoints, and no bath is formulated from raw chemicals
the piece arrives identified and prepared by the upstream preparation line, so this KB begins at the first deposited layer and assumes a clean, activated, water-break-passing surface
the shop can measure a finished stack by XRF or by a witness coupon, or can send out for measurement; where no measurement is possible the claim is downgraded rather than assumed

regulated terms (gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold, nickel release) are obligation classes whose current thresholds, scope and test pairings must be verified in the selling jurisdiction before any claim is made

chemical safety obligation classes — segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness — are already met for every bath the stack calls for, and cyanide-bearing and acid chemistries are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain or spill path
exclusions: current density, rectifier setup and verification, surface-area estimation, Faraday-based time-thickness estimation, and current distribution on complex shapes (shielding, auxiliary anodes, high and low current-density zones) — that is the sibling Electrical Control & Thickness Delivery KB; this KB specifies the target thickness of each layer, not the amps and minutes that deliver it

rack versus barrel versus brush selection, wiring and contact-point placement, agitation and part positioning, drag-out management, inter-tank rinse cascade design, post-plate rinse, dry and first-touch handling, and run logging mechanics — that is the sibling Fixturing, Racking & Run Handling KB

gold and support bath selection, make-up, analysis, replenishment, contamination treatment and bath lifecycle economics — that belongs to the Gold Bath Chemistry & Solution Management specialist; here each bath is a purchased system referred to by its class and its TDS

pre-plate cleaning, electrocleaning, pickling, activation, the water-break gate and mechanical finishing (polishing, tumbling, compound choice) — that belongs to the Surface Preparation & Substrate Readiness specialist

final QC acceptance, customer colour matching, defect-cause diagnosis and the execution of strip-and-replate rework — that belongs to the Finish Quality, Colour & Defect Diagnosis specialist; this KB plans the verification that feeds them

legal sign-off on marking and advertising claims, waste characterization and disposal, and interpretation of jurisdiction rules — that belongs to the Plating Safety, Waste & Compliance specialist; this KB flags the obligation class and escalates

invented bath setpoints (temperature, pH, metal concentration, current density, dwell time), invented prices, guaranteed wear-life figures and asserted numeric regulatory thresholds; parameters appear as mechanisms, published handbook-class ranges named as such, or qualitative bands
mains-side electrical work and any modification of rectifier or equipment outside the manufacturer's instructions
personalized legal, medical or financial advice; nickel-allergy and chemical-exposure questions route to regulation classes and to professional care
dry coating routes (PVD, ALD, parylene) except as named out-of-scope alternative classes that a stack decision may hand off to

competency_questions.question: What has to be written down about this job before I choose a single layer, and what does a complete stack specification contain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACK_DESIGN_BRIEF lists the inputs (substrate, wear, skin contact, forming plan, market claim) and the per-layer output format — layer, purpose, target thickness, verification method

competency_questions.question: Which base metal am I actually building on, and how does that single answer fork the whole stack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBSTRATE_STACK_FORK names the common jewelry substrate classes and states, for each, the mandatory first layer and the trap that a wrong identification causes

competency_questions.question: How thick and how hard must the gold be for the way this particular piece will be worn, and what am I allowed to tell the customer about it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAR_CLASS_SPEC maps piece geometry and use to a gold class as a band, and GOLD_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE explains flash versus build versus hard-gold character and the disclosure that goes with each

competency_questions.question: This piece sits against skin — may nickel appear anywhere in the stack, and if not, what carries the barrier duty instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICKEL_RELEASE_COMPLIANCE states the obligation class, the wear-simulation-then-release test pairing and the verify-your-jurisdiction rule, and NICKEL_FREE_BARRIER_CLASS names palladium and white bronze as the nickel-free replacements with their real costs

competency_questions.question: Why does thin gold laid straight onto brass or sterling go dull and blotchy within weeks, and which layer actually stops it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIFFUSION_BARRIER_RATIONALE explains interdiffusion of the base metal through thin gold and the barrier's two jobs, and PORE_CORROSION_PATH explains the galvanic pore mechanism and why underplate quality dominates it

competency_questions.question: Do I need a strike on this piece, which strike, and what exactly goes wrong if I skip it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STRIKE_LAYER_DESIGN distinguishes the passive-metal nickel strike with live entry, the copper strike before acid baths, and the gold strike, and names the immersion-deposit failure that skipping produces

competency_questions.question: Nickel, palladium, white bronze or copper underneath — how do I choose between the barrier classes, and what does each one commit my shop to?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICKEL_UNDERPLATE_CLASS, NICKEL_FREE_BARRIER_CLASS and COPPER_LEVELING_UNDERPLATE give each class its property profile and its limits, and STACK_SAFETY_ROUTING names the hazard and segregation obligations each chemistry brings into the shop

competency_questions.question: The budget will not fund everything — how do I split the microns between underplate and gold, and what gives way first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THICKNESS_BUDGET_ALLOCATION states the barrier-minimum-first rule and the consequence that the class and the claim change rather than the barrier, and DUPLEX_MULTILAYER_SYSTEMS shows which layer combinations buy which property

competency_questions.question: What has to happen between one layer and the next so the interface actually bonds, and how long may a half-built stack wait?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERFACE_CONTINUITY_TIMING gives the live-entry, no-dry-out, hold-time and reactivation rules per interface, and INTERLAYER_COMPATIBILITY names which layer may not follow which because of drag-in poisoning

competency_questions.question: A sterling piece is to be sold as vermeil — what stack does it need and what must be true before that word is used?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SILVER_VERMEIL_STACK explains silver migration and tarnish read-through, prescribes a nickel-free barrier route, and ties the word vermeil to a verified jurisdiction rule plus a measured gold thickness

competency_questions.question: The piece is stainless, spring steel or zinc die-cast rather than brass — what changes in the stack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STEEL_STAINLESS_STACK covers the live-entry strike on passive metal, the barrier over iron and the embrittlement-bake flag on hardened parts, and ZINC_DIECAST_POROUS_STACK covers protective strike, sealing copper and the not-plateable escalation

competency_questions.question: There is already plating on this piece — do I strip it or build on it, and what does the old layer do to my new stack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPLATE_OVER_EXISTING gives the strip-versus-plate-over decision inputs, the aged-passive-nickel reactivation rule, and the documented-approval requirement for irreversible stripping of customer goods

competency_questions.question: Should this piece get an anti-tarnish dip or a clear topcoat, and what will that never fix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOPCOAT_CLASS_SELECTION separates molecular, wax, electrophoretic, sol-gel and lacquer classes by what each buys and costs, enforces topcoat-last sequencing, and states that a coating is not a nickel-release compliance strategy nor a substitute for gold thickness

competency_questions.question: How do I prove that the stack on the piece is the stack I designed, and what must the job record hold before the shop repeats a claim like gold plated, vermeil or nickel-free?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACK_VERIFICATION_PLAN names the measurement classes with their limits and the witness-coupon practice, and STACK_RECORD_AND_CLAIM lists the as-built record fields and the rule that an unsupported claim is refused and escalated rather than softened

glossary.definition: A very thin, deliberately low-efficiency, high-throwing first deposit whose purpose is adhesion and activation rather than thickness; published practice puts strikes in the sub-micron band. It bonds to a freshly activated surface and gives the next bath a metal it can plate onto.

The layer between substrate and gold whose job is to block interdiffusion of base-metal atoms into the gold, to level the surface, and to carry corrosion duty so the gold layer can stay economically thin; nickel, palladium, white bronze and (capped) copper are the common classes.

Two layers of related metals chosen for complementary properties rather than one thicker layer — for example a ductile copper under a nickel barrier on steel, or semi-bright under bright nickel — where the pair delivers a property neither layer gives alone.

Solid-state migration of base-metal atoms (copper and zinc from brass, silver from sterling, iron from steel) into and through a thin gold deposit over time, accelerated by heat and by thinner gold; it surfaces as dulling, blotching and a tarnish film that polishing removes together with the gold.

The unavoidable pinholes in a thin electrodeposit; because gold is noble relative to everything beneath it, each pore becomes a tiny galvanic cell in which the exposed underlayer corrodes preferentially, showing as spots, halos or salts. Underplate quality dominates the pore count far more than gold thickness does.

The published thickness class systems for decorative gold (ASTM B488 and ISO 27874 class practice) distinguish a flash or decorative band well below a micron, a mid plated band, and heavier micron-class builds for daily wear; the class chosen is a promise about wear, so it belongs in the disclosure as much as in the process sheet.

A marking term class for gold over a sterling or fine silver base with a minimum gold thickness, and in some jurisdictions constraints on what may sit between the silver and the gold; both the threshold and the constraints must be verified in the selling jurisdiction before the word is used.

An obligation class for articles in prolonged skin contact, in which the article's nickel release is measured after a simulated wear-and-corrosion step rather than on a freshly finished surface; the EU family (EN 12472 wear simulation feeding EN 1811 release measurement under the REACH Annex XVII restriction) is the best-known example, and current limits, scope and equivalents must be checked in the market of sale.

A copper-tin-zinc alloy deposit class sold as a proprietary system, used as a bright white nickel-free barrier under gold; hard and comparatively brittle, tinting a flash-thin gold, and dependent on supplier analysis and TDS control rather than shop improvisation.

A high-chloride, high-acid nickel strike used on passive metals such as stainless and aged nickel; entered with current already flowing so the passive film is stripped and overplated in the same instant, since the film reforms in seconds if the surface is left bare in air or in a long rinse.

nodes.definition: Before any tank is switched on, turn the job into a written layer-stack specification: what the piece is made of and on what evidence, how it will actually be worn, whether it sits against skin, whether it will be bent or sized after plating, and what word the seller intends to use at the till. The output is a short table — every layer in order with its purpose, its target thickness band and the method that will verify it — plus the wear expectation the shop is prepared to disclose. A stack that exists only in the plater's head cannot be quoted, repeated by a second operator, defended after a complaint, or improved from logged history.

included: the per-layer written specification for one job
the sale claim and wear expectation the stack must support
the verification method attached to each layer
excluded: bath setpoints and rectifier settings
racking, agitation and run execution
the intake decision to accept, refuse or refer the piece

pros.claim: A written stack makes a job repeatable and quotable instead of a fresh improvisation at the tank each time
pros.example: a repeat trade order of forty brass earring findings is re-run from last quarter's spec sheet, same barrier class and same gold band, instead of being redesigned from memory

cons.claim: Writing the spec costs bench minutes on trivial jobs and tempts the shop to paste a stale default onto a piece that has changed
cons.example: reusing the brass-earring spec on a sterling ring, where silver migration and a vermeil claim make the nickel barrier and the gold band both wrong

failure_modes: carrying the stack only in the plater's memory so the second operator guesses at the barrier
specifying the gold thickness while leaving the underplate unnamed
writing a stack around chemistry the shop does not actually run in-house
acceptance_tests: the spec names every layer in order with its purpose, target thickness band and verification method
the spec states the sale claim and the wear expectation the stack is intended to support
revisit_triggers: the customer changes the intended use, the market of sale or the wording of the claim
the shop adds or retires a barrier or gold system the default stack assumed

base.update_signal: a job of this class returns as a warranty complaint, or the shop's available barrier and gold systems change

nodes.definition: One answer — what the piece is made of — forks everything that follows. Brass and jeweler's bronze need a diffusion barrier but tolerate a direct barrier entry; sterling and fine silver bring migration and tarnish problems and usually a nickel-free requirement; mild steel must never enter an acid metal bath bare and needs both strike and barrier; stainless is passive and needs a live-entry strike; zinc die-cast is porous and chemically fragile; previously plated work is an unknown stack until proven. The fork is taken on verified identity from the intake and preparation line — hallmark, magnet, weight and spot-test classes — never on colour, because a stainless piece run as mild steel loses the entire run and a plated-brass piece taken for solid silver loses the customer's trust.

included: substrate classes a jewelry bench meets and the first layer each demands
the consequence of a wrong fork
the handoff point where identity must already be verified
excluded: the test methods themselves and the accept-refuse-refer triage, which belong to the preparation specialist
cleaning and pickling severity per substrate

pros.claim: Forking on verified substrate class prevents the single most expensive stack error, which is running the wrong first layer
pros.example: recognizing a stainless clasp before the run so it goes to a live-entry nickel strike instead of an acid pickle and a direct gold entry

cons.claim: Real pieces are mixed-metal assemblies, so a single fork can be wrong for part of the same item
cons.example: a brass cuff with a stainless spring pin and a silver solder seam, where one stack cannot be ideal for all three

failure_modes: assuming substrate from colour or from the customer's description
ignoring a solder seam or a repair of a different alloy inside the piece
treating previously plated work as bare substrate
acceptance_tests: the job record names the substrate class and the evidence it rests on before the first layer is chosen
mixed-metal pieces are flagged with the component that constrains the stack
revisit_triggers: the piece behaves unexpectedly in the first tank, for example gassing, etching or refusing to wet
a hidden repair, filler or second alloy is exposed during processing

base.update_signal: a substrate class starts arriving in volumes the current fork does not cover, or a test method reclassifies a family of incoming work

nodes.definition: Classify the piece by the abrasion, sweat and handling it will actually meet, because that — not the customer's budget — sets the gold class. Earring posts, pendant faces and display pieces live easily; ring shanks, bracelet links, clasps, chain and anything that meets a desk edge or a keyring live hard; items worn daily against skin see sweat chemistry as well as rubbing. The published class systems (ASTM B488 and ISO 27874 class practice) give the thickness bands to choose between; the shop's own logged returns tell it which band survives its own customers. The class is a promise: choosing it also chooses what may honestly be said about how long the finish will last.

included: mapping piece geometry and use to a gold thickness class as a band
the wear expectation that must be disclosed with each class
identifying the highest-wear zone that governs the class
excluded: the price of each class
measurement of the delivered thickness
customer negotiation and quoting

pros.claim: Setting the wear class before the stack is designed makes the later disclosure honest and the complaint rate predictable
pros.example: classifying a wedding-band replate as daily-wear so it is quoted as a heavy build rather than sold as a flash refresh that will ghost within a season

cons.claim: Wear class is a judgment about a customer's habits that the shop cannot observe, so the band always carries error
cons.example: a pendant classified as light wear that in fact rides on a nurse's lanyard against a badge clip all day

failure_modes: classifying the whole piece by its easiest surface instead of its hardest-worn zone
letting the quoted price choose the wear class
promising a durability the class cannot deliver on any stack
acceptance_tests: the job record names a wear class with the piece zone that governs it
the disclosed wear expectation given to the customer matches the class chosen
revisit_triggers: returns cluster on one piece type sold in a given class
the customer describes a use the class did not anticipate

base.update_signal: logged returns show a class failing earlier or lasting longer than the band assumed for this shop's customers

nodes.definition: For anything in prolonged skin contact, nickel anywhere in the stack puts the finished article into a nickel-release obligation class — and anywhere means the strike, the barrier, a palladium-nickel alloy and a nickel-hardened acid gold, not just the layer the plater thinks of as the underplate. The regime measures release after a simulated wear-and-corrosion step rather than on a fresh surface (the EU pairing of EN 12472 wear simulation feeding EN 1811 release measurement under the REACH Annex XVII restriction family is the best-known example), so a stack that only passes when new does not pass. The decision is binary and made before the barrier tank is chosen: either the stack is nickel-free by design, or nickel-release testing is planned and the current limit, scope and equivalent rules are verified in the market of sale. Customer allergy questions route to the regulation class and to professional care, never to a shop opinion.

included: the binary nickel decision for skin-contact work
every stack position where nickel can hide
the wear-simulation-then-release test pairing as a class
verify-your-jurisdiction discipline
excluded: numeric release limits asserted as fact
medical advice about nickel allergy
final legal sign-off on a compliance claim, which escalates to the compliance specialist

pros.claim: Deciding nickel before the barrier is chosen is the only cheap moment to decide it, because it cannot be undone later without stripping the whole stack
pros.example: a batch of earring hooks for an EU retailer routed to a copper-strike plus white-bronze stack at design time instead of being re-run after the buyer asks for release data

cons.claim: The nickel-free route costs more, runs on proprietary systems and gives up the best-understood barrier the trade has
cons.example: swapping a well-behaved nickel underplate for a palladium class whose metal cost is priced by the gram and whose window is governed entirely by the supplier's data sheet

failure_modes: treating a nickel strike or a nickel-hardened gold as not counting as nickel in the stack
assuming a topcoat converts a nickel stack into a compliant one
quoting a numeric limit from memory instead of checking the current rule for the market of sale
acceptance_tests: every skin-contact job carries an explicit nickel or nickel-free decision naming the jurisdiction rule consulted and the date it was consulted
no nickel-free claim is recorded unless every layer in the as-built stack, strike and gold alloy included, is nickel-free
revisit_triggers: the piece's market of sale changes or a trade customer starts exporting
the regulation class or its test pairing is revised, or a supplier changes the alloy of a purchased system

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction revises its skin-contact nickel rules or test pairing, or a purchased system's declaration reveals nickel where the stack assumed none

nodes.definition: A stack drawing is also a shopping list of chemistries, and each one drags obligation classes into the shop with it. A cyanide-bearing copper or gold strike commits the shop to absolute segregation from every acid — never mixed, never stored together, never sharing a drain or a spill path — plus locked storage, labeling, trained operators and emergency readiness before the first litre arrives. Nickel baths carry sensitizer and inhalable-carcinogen classes that rule out unmanaged air agitation and casual handling. Proprietary white bronze and palladium systems carry their own handling, analysis and waste obligations. The design lever is that choosing a non-cyanide route deletes a hazard rather than managing it. Everything here is an obligation class plus a formal-training pointer, and the workplace and hazardous-materials rules of your own jurisdiction govern.

included: the hazard and segregation classes each candidate layer brings
the non-cyanide substitution as a hazard-deleting design choice
the rule that a stack requiring chemistry the shop cannot run safely is routed out or redesigned
excluded: written procedures for handling, spill response or destruct treatment, which are the safety specialist's territory
waste characterization and disposal routing
any improvised chemistry or procedure

pros.claim: Testing a stack against the shop's real safety capability at design time prevents a job that cannot be run safely from ever reaching the tanks
pros.example: declining a cyanide copper strike in a single-room shop that shares one drain with the acid bench, and specifying a purchased non-cyanide alkaline copper system instead

cons.claim: The safest route is not always the best-performing one, so hazard avoidance can cost deposit quality or add cost
cons.example: a purchased non-cyanide copper strike that needs tighter control than the classical cyanide strike it replaces on zinc die-cast

failure_modes: designing a stack around chemistry the shop cannot store, segregate or ventilate
adding a nickel bath with air agitation and no mist control
treating hazard classes as an appendix to the process sheet rather than a constraint on the design
acceptance_tests: every bath the stack calls for exists in-house under its own obligation class, or the job is routed out
no designed route places a cyanide-bearing chemistry and an acid chemistry in shared storage, shared drainage or an adjacent unsegregated tank sequence
revisit_triggers: the shop adds, moves or retires a tank, or the bench layout changes
a jurisdiction rule, insurance condition or training lapse changes what may be run

base.update_signal: a change in shop layout, ventilation, training status or jurisdiction rules alters which chemistries may be run

nodes.definition: Thin gold laid straight onto brass, sterling or steel fails from underneath. Copper and zinc from brass, silver from sterling and iron from steel migrate into and through the gold over weeks and months — faster when the piece is warm and much faster when the gold is thin — and arrive at the surface as dulling, blotchy patches and a tarnish film that polishing removes together with the gold. The barrier underplate interposes a metal the base does not readily diffuse through and simultaneously carries corrosion duty, which is what lets the gold layer stay economically thin. The design consequence is the rule the whole subdomain turns on: the thinner the gold, the more completely the stack depends on the barrier beneath it.

included: the interdiffusion mechanism per common substrate
the barrier's two duties, diffusion blocking and corrosion life
why thin gold multiplies barrier dependence
excluded: which specific barrier class to buy, which is the barrier-class nodes' work
bath chemistry that produces the barrier
colour and appearance judgment

pros.claim: Understanding diffusion as the failure mechanism moves the fix to the right layer instead of to more gold
pros.example: a brass cuff that dulled in six weeks is re-specified with a proper barrier rather than by doubling the gold, which would have delayed the same failure at twice the metal cost

cons.claim: Diffusion is slow and invisible at handover, so the cost of omitting a barrier lands months later on someone else's complaint
cons.example: a batch that passed every bench check on the day and came back as returns the following season

failure_modes: plating gold directly onto brass or silver for speed on 'just a quick job'
answering a diffusion complaint with more gold instead of a barrier
ignoring that a warm shop, a polishing motor or a bake step accelerates the mechanism
acceptance_tests: every stack over a diffusing substrate names the barrier layer and states what it blocks
flash-class gold is never specified over bare brass, silver or steel
revisit_triggers: a piece class returns with dulling or blotching rather than wear-through
a new substrate alloy enters the shop's work mix

base.update_signal: field returns or a coupon aging trial show diffusion appearing sooner or later than the current barrier rule assumes

nodes.definition: No thin electrodeposit is pore-free, and gold is noble relative to everything under it, so each pinhole becomes a small galvanic cell in which the exposed underlayer corrodes preferentially: dark halos on nickel, green salts on copper and brass, rust dots on steel, sulfide bloom on silver. The pore count is set far more by the underplate's quality, thickness and smoothness and by the substrate's own defects — die-cast porosity, polishing pits, contact marks — than by the gold on top. Exposure-test classes exist to count pores (nitric vapour and the ASTM B735 and B799 test families), and the practical bench conclusion is blunt: fixing the underlayer beats adding gold microns, and sealing with a topcoat treats the symptom rather than the cause.

included: the pore corrosion mechanism and its visible signatures
what actually controls pore count in a stack
porosity test classes as verification options
excluded: diagnosing a specific defect on a returned piece, which is the finish-quality specialist's work
bath-side causes of roughness and pitting
topcoat application detail

pros.claim: Naming porosity as an underplate property stops the shop from buying gold to solve a problem gold cannot solve
pros.example: a spotted steel keyring fixed by a smoother, thicker nickel barrier rather than by a second gold pass over the same rough underlayer

cons.claim: Porosity is invisible at handover and its tests are destructive or send-out, so it is easy to defer and never measure
cons.example: a shop that has never run a pore test on its standard stack and therefore cannot tell whether its barrier band is adequate

failure_modes: blaming the gold bath for spotting that starts at the substrate or the underplate
sealing a porous stack with lacquer and calling it solved
plating over polishing pits and contact marks that guarantee pore sites
acceptance_tests: the stack for a corrosion-exposed piece names how pore protection is achieved, by barrier thickness, by an added layer or by a sealing class
a periodic pore or exposure test result exists for the shop's standard stacks
revisit_triggers: spotting or bloom appears on pieces whose gold thickness measures on target
a substrate or finishing change alters the surface roughness entering the barrier tank

base.update_signal: an exposure or pore test on the shop's standard stack, or a cluster of spotting returns with on-target thickness

nodes.definition: The strike is a thin, deliberately low-efficiency, high-throwing first deposit whose job is bonding and activation, not thickness; published practice keeps strikes in the sub-micron band. Three cases recur on a jewelry bench. A Wood's-type nickel strike is entered live, with current already flowing, on passive metals such as stainless and aged nickel, so the oxide film is stripped and overplated in the same instant. A copper strike — classical cyanide or a purchased non-cyanide alkaline system — goes on steel and zinc die-cast so the piece never meets an acid metal bath bare. A gold strike bonds the gold layer to the barrier and seals it before the build. Skip the strike and the piece delivers the classic beginner's failure: a dark, spongy immersion deposit formed by displacement, with essentially zero adhesion, that looks plated until it is touched.

included: which strike class each substrate demands
live entry as a mechanism on passive metal
the displacement or immersion deposit failure and how the strike prevents it
excluded: strike bath make-up, analysis and replenishment
the current and dwell that deliver the strike
cleaning and activation before the strike

pros.claim: A correct strike converts adhesion from a hope into a designed interface, at a metal cost close to nothing
pros.example: a stainless clasp struck live in a nickel strike and carried straight on, so the finished piece survives a wrap test instead of peeling in the customer's hand

cons.claim: Each strike adds a tank, a transfer and a timing constraint, and a weak or depleted strike is worse than obvious failure because it fails silently
cons.example: a strike whose acid content has drifted down still deposits something, so the batch passes a tape test and fails on the first bend

failure_modes: dead entry into a strike on passive metal, so the film reforms before deposition starts
dropping bare steel or zinc straight into an acid metal bath
leaving a long rinse or a queue between the strike and the next layer
acceptance_tests: every substrate class in the shop's routing has its strike named, including the live-entry requirement where it applies
an adhesion test class is passed on a coupon or sacrificial piece for each new substrate and strike pairing
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures appear on one substrate class
the strike system is replaced or its supplier changes the product

base.update_signal: coupon adhesion results shift for a substrate class, or the strike product or its data sheet changes

nodes.definition: Nickel is a class of barriers, not one bath. Bright, Watts-type nickel levels and mirrors the surface but carries sulfur from its brightener package, which makes it harder and more brittle; semi-bright sits between; sulfamate nickel is near-stress-free and ductile and is the right choice whenever the piece will be bent, sized or formed after plating. Decorative jewelry practice in the ASTM B488 and ISO 27874 class puts the underplate in the low-single-digit micron band beneath thin gold, with the barrier carrying the corrosion life the gold cannot. Nickel is the cheapest, best-understood and most diffusion-resistant barrier the trade has — and it is also the layer that pulls a skin-contact article into the nickel-release obligation class, which is exactly why that decision is taken before this one.

included: bright, semi-bright and sulfamate nickel as design choices with different mechanical character
the decorative underplate thickness band as published class practice
the compliance flag that travels with any nickel layer
excluded: nickel bath control, analysis and replenishment
numeric nickel-release limits
the electrical delivery of the nickel thickness

pros.claim: Nickel gives the most barrier performance per unit cost and per micron of any common underplate, and levels the surface as a bonus in its bright form
pros.example: a brass pendant whose fine polishing lines disappear under a bright nickel underplate, so the gold above reads as a mirror without further wheel work

cons.claim: Nickel buys performance with a compliance liability on skin-contact goods and with brittleness in its brightest, most levelling form
cons.example: a bright-nickel-under-gold bangle that cracks its stack along the bend when the customer asks for it to be resized

failure_modes: using bright nickel under a piece that will be formed or sized afterwards
specifying nickel on skin-contact goods without the compliance decision on record
treating a nickel strike as sufficient barrier thickness
acceptance_tests: the nickel variant is chosen explicitly for the mechanical duty of the piece, ductile where the piece will be worked
the underplate thickness target is stated and verified by measurement or witness coupon rather than assumed from time in the tank
revisit_triggers: the piece class starts being resized or reworked after plating
the market of sale changes and the compliance decision must be retaken

base.update_signal: coupon bend results or measured underplate thickness disagree with the chosen nickel variant and band

nodes.definition: When the compliance decision forbids nickel, the barrier duty moves to palladium and to white bronze, usually over a copper strike. Palladium and palladium alloys give a hard, white, diffusion-resistant barrier — but a palladium-nickel alloy does not qualify as nickel-free, a trap that catches shops buying on the word palladium alone. White bronze, a copper-tin-zinc deposit class, is the volume nickel-free answer: bright white, hard, comparatively brittle, and sold as a proprietary system whose window, additive control and analysis service belong to the supplier's data sheet rather than to shop improvisation. Both read bright white and therefore tint a flash-thin gold, and both change the shop's economics: palladium is a platinum-group metal priced by the gram, white bronze carries system and analysis cost.

included: palladium and white bronze as barrier classes with their property and cost profiles
the palladium-nickel alloy trap
the proprietary-system dependency these routes create
excluded: operating windows and analysis procedures, which come from the supplier's data sheet
the compliance rule itself
colour matching of the finished gold

pros.claim: A nickel-free barrier keeps skin-contact goods inside the compliance class without giving up diffusion protection
pros.example: a copper strike plus white bronze under gold on a batch of earring hooks destined for a market with a skin-contact nickel restriction

cons.claim: These routes are proprietary, dearer and less forgiving, and their hardness costs ductility on pieces that get bent
cons.example: white bronze under gold on a thin bangle, where the stack crazes at the bend and the shop discovers it has no in-house analysis for the bath

failure_modes: buying a palladium-nickel system for a nickel-free job
running a proprietary barrier without the supplier's analysis service and drifting out of window unnoticed
specifying a hard white barrier under flash gold and getting a pale, washed-out colour
acceptance_tests: the purchased system's declaration confirms the deposit contains no nickel before it is used on a nickel-free job
a coupon from the nickel-free stack is measured and bend-tested before customer work runs on it
revisit_triggers: the supplier reformulates the system or its data sheet changes
metal price or lead time makes the chosen nickel-free route unviable for the piece class

base.update_signal: a supplier data-sheet revision, a composition declaration, or coupon results from the shop's own nickel-free trials

nodes.definition: Copper's job in a stack is levelling and ductility, not barrier duty. A bright acid copper build fills polishing scratches, micro-pits and casting texture so the finish is made in the tank rather than on the wheel, which matters most on castings and on customer pieces where every pass of the polishing motor removes irreplaceable metal. A ductile copper interlayer also absorbs bending strain that would crack a hard barrier above it. Two rules bound its use: copper diffuses into gold readily, so copper is never the last layer under thin gold and must always be capped by a proper barrier; and on steel or zinc it is preceded by an alkaline copper strike, because bare steel dropped into acid copper gives a loose displacement film rather than a deposit.

included: copper as a levelling and ductility layer
the always-cap rule and the strike-before-acid-copper rule
levelling in the tank as an alternative to further mechanical finishing
excluded: copper bath chemistry and its cyanide or non-cyanide safety class detail
mechanical polishing technique
the customer sign-off procedure for irreversible metal work

pros.claim: Levelling with copper saves substrate metal on pieces that cannot afford further polishing
pros.example: a worn cast ring where a copper build and a light cut-back restores a smooth face without thinning a hallmark or softening the detail

cons.claim: Copper adds thickness, cost and an extra interface, and polishing between layers is skilled bench time that can go wrong on a customer's piece
cons.example: a heavy copper build cut back too enthusiastically, exposing bare substrate at a high point that must then be re-plated from the strike

failure_modes: leaving copper as the layer directly under a thin gold and watching it diffuse through
entering acid copper on bare steel or zinc without a strike
building copper thick enough to blur the detail the customer valued
acceptance_tests: every copper layer in a stack is followed by a barrier layer before any gold
polishing between plated layers on a customer's piece has documented approval before it is performed
revisit_triggers: the incoming surface finish changes so the levelling requirement changes
a copper-containing stack shows diffusion or bleed-through at the gold

base.update_signal: measured results or returns showing copper levelling either unnecessary or insufficient for the incoming finish of this work class

nodes.definition: Real stacks are combinations chosen for how the layers behave together. Copper under nickel on mild steel puts ductility below the barrier so the pair survives bending that nickel alone would crack. Semi-bright under bright nickel lengthens the corrosion path through the underplate rather than adding raw thickness. Copper strike under white bronze is the standard nickel-free skin-contact route. A gold strike under a gold build gives the colour layer a bonded gold interface to grow on. The design discipline is arithmetic of cost, not enthusiasm: every added layer buys a named property and costs an interface, a tank, a transfer, a rinse and a queue slot in which the stack can go wrong — so a layer that cannot name the property it buys does not belong in the stack.

included: the standard duplex combinations and the property each buys
the earn-its-interface test for adding a layer
the cost of a layer in tanks, transfers and queue exposure
excluded: thickness allocation arithmetic across the stack
tank sequencing and rinse design between the layers
bath-side control of each layer

pros.claim: Duplex stacks deliver combinations of ductility, levelling and corrosion path that no single layer of any thickness provides
pros.example: ductile copper under a thin ductile nickel on a steel-wire piece that will be coiled after plating, where a single bright nickel of the same total thickness would crack

cons.claim: Every extra layer is another interface that can fail and another queue in which a surface can passivate or dry
cons.example: a four-layer stack that has to wait for one shared rectifier, so the barrier sits wet in a rinse long enough to need reactivation before the gold

failure_modes: adding layers by habit without naming the property each buys
designing a stack with more tank steps than the shop can run without a hold
combining a hard layer over a soft one in a way that cracks under bending
acceptance_tests: each layer in the stack has a stated purpose that a simpler stack would not deliver
the full sequence is runnable in the shop's tank line without an unplanned hold between layers
revisit_triggers: the shop's tank line, rectifier capacity or throughput changes
a stack fails at a specific interface rather than in a layer

base.update_signal: failure analysis locating a failure at an interface, or a change in the shop's ability to run multi-tank sequences without holds

nodes.definition: The gold is itself an architecture rather than a single coat: a gold strike bonds and seals the barrier, a build layer carries thickness where the wear class demands it, and the visible layer carries colour and hardness. Flash-class deposits in the published ASTM B488 and ISO 27874 class practice sit well below a micron and depend entirely on the layers beneath them for corrosion life; heavier micron-class builds buy wear, not beauty. Alloy-hardened acid golds resist abrasion far better than soft near-pure deposits, but the hardener matters to more than hardness — a nickel-hardened gold is a nickel-bearing layer for compliance purposes. And below roughly a couple of tenths of a micron the underlayer's colour reads through, so a white barrier makes a thin gold look pale and a copper-rich underlayer warms it.

included: gold strike, build and colour layers as separate design roles
flash versus build class as a wear decision
hard versus soft gold character and the hardener's compliance implication
colour read-through at very thin gold
excluded: gold bath family selection and karat colour chemistry, which belong to the bath specialist
colour matching to a customer reference, which belongs to the finish-quality specialist
the amps and minutes that deliver the thickness

pros.claim: Separating the gold into strike, build and colour roles lets the shop buy wear and colour independently instead of paying for both in one thick layer
pros.example: a hard gold build for wear with a thin soft colour flash on top to hit the customer's warm hue, rather than a single thick soft deposit that wears in a month

cons.claim: More gold layers mean more baths, more drag-out of the most expensive chemistry in the shop and more chance of a colour mismatch between passes
cons.example: a two-bath gold route where the colour flash from a different system reads greener than the retained master under shop lighting

failure_modes: specifying flash gold for a wear class that needs a build
forgetting that a nickel-hardened gold counts as nickel in a skin-contact stack
blaming a pale colour on the gold bath when the cause is read-through from a white barrier under too-thin gold
acceptance_tests: the gold layers are specified by role with a target thickness band each, and the total meets the wear class
the hardener class of any hard gold used on skin-contact work is checked against the nickel decision
revisit_triggers: colour drifts on a stack whose gold thickness measures on target
the wear class or the claim for the piece changes

base.update_signal: measured thickness and colour results from the shop's own coupons, or a change in the gold systems available on the line

nodes.definition: Every job has a finite budget of money, tank time and gold, so the plater allocates microns across the stack rather than maximizing one layer. The mechanism runs in a fixed order: the barrier takes its minimum for the substrate and the wear class first, because it carries diffusion and corrosion duty; the gold then takes what the wear class and the intended claim require; and if the remaining budget cannot fund that gold, the class and the claim change — never the barrier. Gold consumption scales with plated area times thickness, which is what makes a modest gold over a sound barrier the honest economy play and a thick gold over nothing the expensive mistake. The allocation is written as target bands with the method that will verify each, not as a promise.

included: the barrier-minimum-first allocation rule
area times thickness as the gold cost mechanism
the rule that the claim gives way before the barrier does
excluded: the surface-area estimation method and the Faraday arithmetic that converts thickness into time, which are the electrical-control sibling's work
job pricing and quotation
measurement execution

pros.claim: An explicit allocation turns a vague budget conversation into a defensible engineering decision with a named casualty
pros.example: telling a trade customer that the same money buys either a compliant barrier plus a flash gold sold as decorative, or a thinner barrier the shop will not build

cons.claim: Allocation depends on cost inputs that move, so a rule tuned at one gold price can misallocate at another
cons.example: a standing stack recipe whose gold band was set when metal was cheaper and which now prices the shop out of a routine job

failure_modes: thinning the barrier to fund a gold thickness the customer asked for by name
quoting a micron figure the shop has never measured on that piece geometry
treating the calculated thickness as the delivered thickness
acceptance_tests: the stack states a target band for every layer and the verification method for each
when the budget forces a reduction, the record shows the class and claim changed rather than the barrier
revisit_triggers: measurement shows a layer landing outside its target band
metal cost or the customer's price point moves enough to change the allocation

base.update_signal: measured layer thicknesses from finished jobs, or a material change in metal cost or in the shop's throughput cost

nodes.definition: Every interface in a stack has a clock running against it. A freshly struck stainless surface repassivates in seconds if it is left in air or parked in a long rinse. A plated nickel surface goes passive as it sits, in air and even standing in water, so a barrier that waited overnight will shed the gold that follows unless it is reactivated. Work that dries between tanks carries flash oxide and rinse residue into the next layer. The rules that follow are unglamorous and decisive: current on before immersion where the chemistry demands live entry, wet transfers with no dry-out, a stated maximum hold between layers, and an acid reactivation dip for anything that has waited. The penalty is not visible on the day — it appears at the bend test, or on the customer's finger.

included: live entry, wet transfer, hold limits and reactivation as interface rules
the passivation clock on nickel and on stainless
what to do with a stack that has waited
excluded: rinse tank design, cascade layout and drag-out economics, which belong to the run-handling sibling
cleaning chemistry
adhesion testing method detail

pros.claim: Explicit interface rules convert the most common invisible defect, delayed peeling, into a scheduling constraint anyone on the bench can follow
pros.example: a written rule that a nickel-plated batch left past the hold limit goes back through an activation dip before the gold tank, no exceptions for a late courier

cons.claim: Timing rules bind the shop's schedule and can force a re-run when a rectifier fault or a lunch break interrupts a stack mid-build
cons.example: a barrier-plated batch stranded by a power interruption that must be reactivated or stripped rather than simply finished after the break

failure_modes: letting a plated barrier dry or sit overnight and plating gold onto it unreactivated
dead entry where live entry is required
a long rinse between the strike and the layer it was struck for
acceptance_tests: every interface in the written stack carries its entry rule and a maximum hold time
held work is reactivated or re-struck before the next layer, and the hold is noted in the job record
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures correlate with interrupted or queued runs
the line's throughput or staffing changes the realistic time between tanks

base.update_signal: peel or blister failures traced to specific holds, or a bend-test result after a deliberately held coupon

nodes.definition: Adjacent layers constrain each other chemically, so the stack order is not free. Nickel carried into an acid gold bath is a listed poison of that chemistry; chloride dragged from a strike attacks some gold systems; silicate from an alkaline cleaner gels when it meets acid and leaves a film that later peels like paint; and a cyanide-bearing chemistry adjacent to an acid one is a safety line, not a process preference. The architecture decision this node owns is which layer may follow which, and where the sequence needs an extra separation step, a dedicated dead rinse or a different chemistry choice altogether. How that rinse is plumbed, cascaded and costed belongs to the run-handling sibling; what the sequence must not do belongs here.

included: chemical adjacency constraints between layers
the point in the sequence where a separation must exist
the cyanide-acid adjacency line as an absolute
excluded: rinse cascade design, water use and drag-out recovery economics
bath contamination treatment and recovery
safety procedure text

pros.claim: Checking adjacency at design time protects the most expensive bath in the shop from the cheapest mistake in the line
pros.example: spotting that a proposed barrier-to-gold sequence would carry nickel straight into the acid gold, and inserting a dedicated separation step before the run

cons.claim: Compatibility constraints add steps and tanks, and they are invisible until a bath is already degraded
cons.example: a shop that discovers its gold bath has been slowly poisoned only when deposits go dull across every job, weeks after the sequence changed

failure_modes: sequencing a barrier directly into a sensitive gold bath with no separation
assuming a single rinse handles every transition equally
letting a tank-space constraint dictate an unsafe or incompatible adjacency
acceptance_tests: each transition in the written sequence names what it must not carry forward
no cyanide-bearing and acid chemistry pair appears adjacent without the segregation the safety class requires
revisit_triggers: a bath shows contamination symptoms after a sequence change
a new chemistry joins the line or a tank is relocated

base.update_signal: bath analysis or deposit symptoms indicating drag-in from a specific upstream layer, or a supplier compatibility note

nodes.definition: Sterling and fine silver are the hardest common substrate for thin gold. Silver migrates readily into and through a gold deposit, surfacing as a haze that reads to the customer as a bad gold job within weeks, and silver's own sulfide tarnish blooms at every pore in the layer above it. Vermeil is additionally a regulated marking class: a silver base and a minimum gold thickness are typically required, and jurisdictions differ on what may sit between the silver and the gold, so the stack must be designed against the rule in the market of sale rather than against shop habit. The practical architecture is a nickel-free barrier — a palladium class, or a copper strike with white bronze — under a gold thickness that meets the class, with the thickness measured before the word vermeil is used anywhere.

included: silver migration and tarnish read-through as the design driver
the nickel-free barrier route over silver
vermeil as a verify-your-jurisdiction marking class tied to measured thickness
excluded: asserting a numeric vermeil threshold as universal fact
legal sign-off on the marking claim
silver cleaning and pre-plate finishing

pros.claim: A barrier over silver is what makes a vermeil piece still look like gold a year later instead of a hazy grey-gold
pros.example: two identical sterling rings, one plated directly and hazy by spring, one with a palladium-class barrier still clean

cons.claim: The compliant route over silver is the most expensive common stack the bench builds, and the rule that governs the word is not the shop's to interpret
cons.example: a nickel-free barrier plus a gold thickness that meets the class on a low-margin sterling charm, where the honest answer may be to sell it as plated rather than as vermeil

failure_modes: plating gold straight onto sterling for speed
using a nickel barrier under a piece to be sold as vermeil without checking whether the rule allows it
using the word vermeil on the strength of a calculated rather than a measured thickness
acceptance_tests: the jurisdiction rule for the vermeil class is checked and the check dated in the job record before the term is used
gold thickness on the piece or on a witness coupon is measured and recorded against the class
revisit_triggers: the seller's market changes or a trade customer resells into another jurisdiction
the marking rule or its thickness class is revised

base.update_signal: a revision of the marking class in a market the shop sells into, or measured aging results from the shop's own silver stacks

nodes.definition: Ferrous work forks hard. Stainless is passive: only a live-entry, high-acid nickel strike of the Wood's type strips the chromium-oxide film and overplates it in the same instant, and a rinse delay afterwards lets the film reform, which is why such a piece can pass a tape test and fail a wrap test. Mild steel must be struck before it meets any acid metal bath and needs a real barrier before gold, because iron diffuses into gold and rusts out through every pore. Spring-tempered and high-carbon parts add a hazard that is mechanical rather than cosmetic: acid and cathodic steps charge hydrogen into the metal and the part can fail days later in the customer's hand, which published practice answers with a low-temperature bake soon after plating in the ASTM B850 and F519 class and with ductile rather than bright barriers wherever the part will be formed.

included: the passive-metal live-entry strike requirement
barrier duty over iron
the hydrogen-embrittlement flag and the bake as published class practice
ductile barrier choice for parts that will be formed
excluded: pickle severity and cleaning chemistry for steel, which belong to the preparation specialist
bake oven operation and equipment instructions
invented bake temperatures or times asserted as universal fact

pros.claim: Treating stainless and hardened steel as their own forks prevents both the classic peel and the far worse delayed mechanical failure
pros.example: a spring clasp routed to a ductile barrier plus a post-plate bake per the standard class rather than to the shop's default bright-nickel stack

cons.claim: The ferrous forks add steps, equipment and timing that a small jewelry bench may not have, which sometimes makes refusal the right answer
cons.example: a shop with no temperature-controlled oven declining spring-steel work rather than plating it and hoping

failure_modes: running stainless through the mild-steel route and losing the whole batch to peeling
rinsing at length after a strike on passive metal
plating hardened parts with no embrittlement control and shipping a delayed failure
acceptance_tests: stainless work passes a bend or wrap adhesion class on a coupon before the batch is released
hardened or spring-tempered parts carry an embrittlement-control step in the job record or are refused
revisit_triggers: an adhesion or breakage failure is reported on ferrous work
the shop starts taking a new ferrous alloy or temper class

base.update_signal: coupon adhesion or wrap results on ferrous work, or a customer report of a part failing mechanically after plating

nodes.definition: Zinc die-cast findings and pot-metal costume pieces punish a standard stack. The substrate itself is attacked by aggressive acid, the casting's porosity holds solution that bleeds out days later and blisters or stains the finish, thin walls hide old solder and filler, and the surface is often rough enough that the finish must be built rather than polished. The architecture answer is a protective alkaline copper strike first — never a bare entry into an acid metal bath — then enough copper to seal and level, then the barrier and the gold. The honest caveat belongs in the same breath: a genuinely porous or previously repaired casting may not be plateable to a durable finish at any thickness, and that conclusion is escalated to intake and the customer rather than forced through the tanks.

included: protective strike and sealing copper on porous castings
bleed-out and blistering as a substrate-driven failure
the escalation when a casting cannot carry a durable finish
excluded: the intake accept-refuse decision itself
mechanical repair or filling of the casting
aggressive stripping chemistry on zinc

pros.claim: A protective strike and a sealing build make otherwise unplatable costume castings viable and keep the substrate out of the acid
pros.example: a vintage cast pendant sealed with copper before the barrier, so entrapped solution never reaches the gold layer

cons.claim: The sealing route costs thickness, time and money on low-value pieces and still cannot rescue the worst castings
cons.example: a pot-metal brooch that blisters a week after a full stack because porosity ran right through the casting

failure_modes: entering acid chemistry with bare zinc and dissolving the substrate
plating over porosity and shipping a piece that blisters after delivery
accepting a casting the shop already knows cannot hold a finish
acceptance_tests: porous or die-cast work carries a protective strike and a sealing layer in the written stack
a piece judged unplatable to a durable finish is escalated with that judgment recorded rather than run
revisit_triggers: blistering or bleed-out appears after delivery on a casting class
a new supplier's castings behave differently in the first tanks

base.update_signal: post-delivery blistering reports, or trial results on a new casting source

nodes.definition: Most jewelry plating is replating, so the real question is what is already on the piece and whether it stays. Worn flash over brass, old gold, rhodium, aged and now-passive nickel and unknown vintage stacks each behave differently: aged nickel must be reactivated or re-struck or the new stack simply peels; plating over a failing layer inherits every one of its defects and hides them for a few weeks; and stripping is chemistry that removes metal, is irreversible on a customer's piece and carries the same hazard classes as plating. When the existing stack cannot be identified, the honest options are a discreet test area, a conservative plate-over with the risk disclosed and documented, or refusal — never a confident promise about a stack nobody has seen the inside of.

included: the strip-versus-plate-over decision inputs
reactivation of aged passive underplate
documented approval and disclosed risk on customer goods
excluded: stripping bath chemistry and execution, which belong to the finish-quality and safety specialists
the intake condition record and photography
pricing of restoration work

pros.claim: Deciding strip-versus-build explicitly stops the shop inheriting an unknown stack's failures as its own warranty problem
pros.example: stripping a flaking old plate on a customer's bangle with written approval rather than laying fresh gold over the flakes and owning the result

cons.claim: Stripping removes metal from a piece that cannot be replaced and can uncover damage the customer blames on the shop
cons.example: stripping a worn plate to find pitting and a soft solder repair underneath that were invisible at intake

failure_modes: plating over an aged passive underplate without reactivation
stripping a customer's piece without documented approval and a condition record
promising a result on a stack whose composition nobody has established
acceptance_tests: every replate job records what was found on the piece and the decision made about it
no stripping of customer goods proceeds without documented approval and a dated condition record
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures cluster on replate work rather than on new work
a test area reveals a stack different from the one assumed at intake

base.update_signal: outcomes of test areas and strip decisions logged across replate jobs, or a rise in replate-specific failures

nodes.definition: Post-plate treatments are a family of classes with different jobs, and choosing among them is a stack decision rather than an afterthought. Molecular anti-tarnish dips — azole chemistry on copper and silver-bearing surfaces, proprietary thiol-type passivates — chemisorb an invisible film that slows tarnish at pores without changing the look or the feel. Waxes add a sub-micron handling and display layer. Electrophoretic clear lacquer deposits a self-limiting continuous film that reaches recesses and covers the thin-gold zones a ring wears through first, at the cost of a cure step, a polymer feel and an aging clock. Sol-gel and sprayed lacquer classes trade hardness against reworkability. Three rules bind all of them: the topcoat goes on last, on the finished formed piece, because every hard film cracks at forming strain; a coating is not a nickel-release compliance strategy, since coated articles are assessed after simulated wear and corrosion; and premium and food-contact surfaces default to honest bare gold.

included: the topcoat classes and what each buys and costs
topcoat-last sequencing
the limits: not a compliance strategy, not a substitute for gold thickness, not for food-contact surfaces by default
excluded: coating application technique, cure schedules and booth practice
coating supplier windows, which come from the data sheet
food-contact clearance determination, which needs a supplier declaration and jurisdiction check

pros.claim: A sealing class lets a modest gold on a sound barrier survive real wear on low-abrasion goods, at a fraction of the cost of the equivalent gold
pros.example: a continuous clear film covering the cut ends and contact flats of a costume ring, exactly where the gold is thinnest and fails first

cons.claim: Every organic topcoat trades away the bare-metal look and feel and starts an aging and yellowing clock, and it can hide rather than fix a weak stack
cons.example: a clear-coated flash job that looks perfect for a season and then shows tarnish underneath an intact film because the surface was contaminated when it was coated

failure_modes: coating a piece that will still be bent, sized or formed
offering a coating as the answer to a nickel-release question
using a topcoat to justify a gold thickness below what the disclosed wear class needs
acceptance_tests: the topcoat decision is recorded with its class and the reason, and it is the last step in the routing
no compliance or thickness claim in the job record rests on the presence of a coating
revisit_triggers: coated pieces return with tarnish under an intact film or with cracked coating at bends
a coating product or its declaration changes

base.update_signal: aging or wear results on coated versus uncoated coupons of the shop's own stacks, or a supplier declaration change

nodes.definition: The plan for proving that the stack on the piece is the stack that was designed is written before the run, not after a complaint. Thickness measurement by X-ray fluorescence in the ISO 3497 and ASTM B568 class reads the gold and can read an underplate, with real limits on very thin strikes, on small or curved features and on complex geometry, which is why a flat witness coupon plated in the same rack position and the same run is the routine proxy and a microsection in the ASTM B487 class is the referee when a number is disputed. Adhesion is proven by bend, wrap, burnish or thermal-shock classes of the ASTM B571 family on a coupon or a sacrificial piece, and porosity by exposure-test classes. The discipline behind all of it: nothing about layer identity, thickness or adhesion is asserted from the recipe alone, and a calculated thickness is an input to be checked, never a result to be reported.

included: measurement and test classes for thickness, adhesion and porosity with their limits
the witness-coupon practice
the rule that calculation is checked by measurement
excluded: the Faraday arithmetic itself, which belongs to the electrical-control sibling
full QC acceptance sampling and release, which belong to the finish-quality specialist
instrument calibration procedure

pros.claim: Planning verification before the run is what makes a coupon exist when it is needed, which is the only cheap way to measure a finished piece
pros.example: a coupon riding the same rack as a batch of pendants, so the underplate thickness can be sectioned later without cutting a customer's piece

cons.claim: Measurement costs money and time and its methods have blind spots that can give false confidence on real geometry
cons.example: an instrument reading taken on a flat pendant face that says nothing about the thin deposit inside a recess or on a wire edge

failure_modes: reporting a calculated thickness as a measured one
measuring only the easiest, highest-current-density surface on the piece
having no coupon and no way to check the underplate after the fact
acceptance_tests: each layer with a target band has a named verification method and a place where it is measured
a witness coupon or an equivalent measurable surface exists for any job carrying a thickness claim
revisit_triggers: measured and calculated thickness diverge repeatedly on one geometry
a customer or trade account disputes a thickness or adhesion result

base.update_signal: divergence between measured and estimated thickness on a geometry class, or the arrival of a new measurement capability

nodes.definition: The stack ends as a record: substrate as verified, every layer with its purchased system, its target band and its measured value, the verification method and the coupon result, the nickel decision with the jurisdiction rule consulted and the date, the topcoat route, and the exact wording the shop is prepared to stand behind at sale. This is what converts a plating job into a defensible claim. Gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold and nickel-free are regulated obligation classes whose current thresholds and scope are verified in the market of sale; plated goods are never represented as solid gold; wear expectations are disclosed before the sale rather than explained after the complaint. Where the record cannot support the claim the customer or the trade account wants, the claim is refused and escalated — the shop changes its words, never its measurements.

included: the as-built record fields
regulated term classes as verify-your-jurisdiction obligations
the refuse-and-escalate rule for unsupported claims
disclosure of wear expectation before sale
excluded: legal sign-off on marking and advertising, which escalates to the compliance specialist
asserting numeric thresholds for any regulated term
the shop's pricing and customer-relationship management

pros.claim: An as-built record is the only artifact that survives a dispute, and it is also the shop's own improvement data
pros.example: a return answered in a minute from the job sheet showing the measured underplate, the measured gold and the coupon adhesion result

cons.claim: Recording discipline costs bench time on every job, and the record can also document the shop's own mistake
cons.example: a job sheet that proves the gold landed below the band the customer was quoted, which the shop must then honour

failure_modes: repeating a customer's preferred term without checking what the record supports
recording targets but never the measured values
letting a trade account's label requirement drive the claim rather than the evidence
acceptance_tests: the record holds substrate, every layer with target and measured values, the verification method, the nickel decision with its dated rule check and the wording to be used at sale
any claim the record cannot support is refused in writing and escalated rather than softened
revisit_triggers: a marking or advertising rule changes in a market the shop sells into
a trade account requests a label the current record cannot support

base.update_signal: a regulator, trade body or buyer changes the evidence expected behind a marking claim, or a dispute exposes a gap in the record fields

edges.why_related: the fork is taken on the substrate identity and evidence the brief captured
the wear class is derived from the use, geometry and skin-contact answers recorded in the brief
the brief's skin-contact answer and market of sale are what trigger the nickel decision
which element will diffuse into the gold is a property of the substrate class chosen at the fork
the substrate class decides whether a strike is required and which strike it must be
the substrate fork determines which chemistries the route will need and therefore which hazard classes come with it
pore corrosion is the second failure the barrier layer exists to control, understood on top of the diffusion mechanism
the nickel class is selected to perform the diffusion-blocking and corrosion duty the mechanism defines
the nickel-free barrier classes are only reached because the compliance decision forbade nickel
copper on steel or zinc is only laid after the strike that prevents a displacement deposit
duplex designs combine nickel variants with other layers, so the nickel class must be understood first
the nickel-free routes are themselves duplex combinations of a copper strike with a white bronze or palladium barrier
the wear class decides whether the gold is a flash, a plated class or a heavy build and whether it must be hard
the gold roles and their bands are one side of the micron allocation
the chosen layer combination fixes how many layers the micron budget must be divided between
live entry and the no-delay rule after a strike are the sharpest cases of the interface clock
compatibility is checked over the specific layer sequence the duplex design produced
every target band allocated is what the verification plan must be able to check
the record's measured values and their methods come out of the verification plan
nickel may only be specified where the skin-contact release class permits it, which is why the compliance decision precedes the barrier choice
a cyanide-bearing strike is only available to a shop that meets the segregation, storage, training and emergency-readiness obligations, otherwise a purchased non-cyanide system is specified
the allocation must meet the wear class or the class and the disclosed expectation change with it
what may sit directly beneath the gold, and what must be separated from it, is constrained by drag-in poisoning of the gold chemistry
a nickel-free claim may only be recorded when every layer including strike and gold alloy is nickel-free and the jurisdiction rule check is dated
palladium and white bronze are proprietary systems whose handling, analysis and waste obligations must be met before the route is available
nickel is the cheapest and best-understood barrier while the nickel-free classes are dearer, more brittle and proprietary, so cost and performance pull against compliance
edges.resolution_rule: for prolonged skin contact the compliance class wins without negotiation: the stack goes nickel-free, the choice and the dated jurisdiction check are recorded, and the extra cost is quoted rather than absorbed by silently reinstating nickel

edges.why_related: the gold the customer wants to see and the barrier the piece needs to survive compete for the same money and the same tank time
edges.resolution_rule: the barrier takes its minimum for the substrate and wear class first; if the remaining budget cannot fund the gold band the claimed class requires, the class and the claim are reduced and disclosed, never the barrier

edges.why_related: a continuous coating suppresses release on a fresh article and is therefore tempting as a shortcut around a nickel-bearing stack
edges.resolution_rule: compliance wins: release is assessed after simulated wear and corrosion, so a coating is never accepted as the compliance strategy; either the stack is nickel-free or testing is planned, and any coating benefit is treated as additional rather than sufficient

edges.why_related: a heavy copper build with polishing between layers is the best levelling tool available and is also irreversible metal work on someone's irreplaceable piece
edges.resolution_rule: on customer goods the minimum-removal default holds: heavy build with cut-back proceeds only on documented approval with a dated condition record, otherwise the piece is finished to the level its current surface allows and the limit is disclosed

edges.why_related: every layer added for performance adds an interface and a queue slot in which a surface can passivate or dry
edges.resolution_rule: a layer is kept only if it names a property a simpler stack cannot deliver and the line can run the sequence without an unplanned hold; where the shop cannot hold the timing, the stack is simplified rather than run with a risky interface

edges.why_related: corrosion at pores is the failure that sealing classes exist to slow, which is why a porous stack is the usual reason a topcoat is considered
silver's migration into gold is what forces the barrier and drives the whole sterling stack design
sealing and levelling copper is the mechanism that makes a porous casting carry a finish at all
the nickel barrier is what stops iron reaching the gold and what carries corrosion life on ferrous work, and its ductile variant is what survives forming
the topcoat decision is taken and applied after the metal stack is complete, because every hard film cracks at forming strain and coating is the last station
the stack is built under its interface rules and only then measured and adhesion-tested against what was specified
measured layer thicknesses on real geometry retune the allocation and expose where the bands were optimistic
as-built records accumulate into the shop's default stacks, so tomorrow's brief starts from what was measured yesterday rather than from habit
both are substrate classes where a bare entry into an acid metal bath gives a worthless displacement deposit or attacks the substrate, so both are strike-first routes rather than the brass default

conflict_axes.name: barrier_performance_versus_nickel_free_compliance
conflict_axes.description: Nickel is the cheapest, most diffusion-resistant and best-understood barrier available, and it is exactly the layer that pulls a skin-contact article into the nickel-release obligation class.
poles: specify the nickel barrier that performs best per unit cost
specify a nickel-free barrier so the article stays inside the compliance class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: skin contact plus the rule of the market of sale settles it: nickel-free wins, the dated jurisdiction check goes in the record, and the cost difference is quoted openly

conflict_axes.name: gold_microns_versus_barrier_microns
conflict_axes.description: The customer sees and pays for gold, while the barrier is what makes the gold last, and both draw on the same budget of money and tank time.
poles: put the budget into visible gold thickness
put the budget into the barrier that carries corrosion and diffusion duty
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: barrier minimum first for the substrate and wear class, gold next, and if the gold band cannot be funded the class and the claim drop rather than the barrier

conflict_axes.name: hardness_and_levelling_versus_ductility
conflict_axes.description: The brightest, most levelling underplates are the hardest and most brittle, while the deposits that survive bending and sizing are softer and level poorly.
poles: choose the hard bright barrier for mirror finish and wear
choose the ductile low-stress barrier so the stack survives forming and sizing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: if the piece will be bent, coiled, sized or set after plating, ductility wins and the finish is achieved before the stack; otherwise the levelling deposit is allowed

conflict_axes.name: sealed_finish_versus_honest_bare_metal
conflict_axes.description: An organic topcoat protects thin gold at pores and worn edges, and it also replaces the feel of bare metal, starts an aging clock and can mask a weak stack.
poles: seal the finish with a continuous coating class
sell honest bare gold at the thickness the wear class needs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: premium, heirloom and food-contact surfaces stay bare and pay in gold thickness; costume and low-abrasion goods may be coated provided the coating is disclosed and never used to justify a thinner claim

conflict_axes.name: cost_economy_versus_disclosed_wear_life
conflict_axes.description: A modest gold over a sound barrier is the legitimate economy play, and the same stack becomes dishonest the moment it is sold with a durability nobody measured.
poles: build to the price the market will pay
build and describe to the wear class the piece will actually meet
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the cheaper stack is allowed, the inflated description is not: disclosure of the wear expectation is a condition of selling the economy stack, and plated goods are never represented as solid gold

conflict_axes.name: strip_and_rebuild_versus_plate_over
conflict_axes.description: Stripping gives a known starting surface and removes irreplaceable metal from a customer's piece; plating over keeps the metal and inherits an unknown stack's defects.
poles: strip to a known substrate and rebuild the stack
plate over the existing layers and keep the metal
