conflict_axes.resolution_hint: identify first with a discreet test area; strip only with documented approval and a dated condition record; where identification fails, disclose the risk of a plate-over in writing or refuse the job

conflict_axes.name: throughput_versus_interface_timing
conflict_axes.description: Batching and queuing between tanks is how a small shop stays profitable, and every hour a half-built stack waits is an interface quietly going passive.
poles: run each stack through its interfaces inside the hold limits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: interface rules win: work held past its limit is reactivated or re-struck before the next layer, and if the schedule cannot support the stack the stack is simplified rather than the rule bent

conflict_axes.name: colour_now_versus_stack_integrity
conflict_axes.description: A very thin gold over a white barrier reads pale, and the fast fixes for that appearance are the ones that damage the stack's honesty or its life.
poles: adjust appearance with a tinted coating or a thinner-still colour flash
add the gold the colour needs and keep the barrier intact
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read-through is solved with gold, not with tint: increase the gold band or accept and disclose the colour the stack gives, and never describe a tinted coating as gold

conflict_axes.name: hazard_avoidance_versus_process_convenience
conflict_axes.description: The classical chemistries are often the most forgiving on difficult substrates, and some of them bring hazard classes a small shop cannot honestly carry.
poles: run the classical chemistry that plates the substrate best
choose the route whose hazards the shop can genuinely control
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety and segregation obligations win: a stack requiring chemistry the shop cannot store, segregate, ventilate and train for is redesigned around a purchased alternative or the job is routed to a shop that can run it

edge_cases.description: A customer asks for nickel-free work on a piece that already carries an old nickel underplate from a previous plating job
edge_cases.trigger: a skin-contact replate arrives with an unknown or known nickel layer already on it
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly that plating over existing nickel does not make the article nickel-free, offer full strip and rebuild with documented approval, or decline the nickel-free description and record why

edge_cases.description: A sterling piece is to be sold as vermeil but the shop's default stack uses a nickel barrier
edge_cases.trigger: a vermeil order enters a line whose standard barrier is nickel
edge_cases.mitigation: check the marking rule for the market of sale before designing, route to a nickel-free barrier, measure the gold against the class, and if either cannot be met sell the piece as gold plated over silver instead

edge_cases.description: Spring-tempered or high-carbon findings are to be plated and then bent into their final shape
edge_cases.trigger: a plate-then-form job on hardened steel wire or spring components
edge_cases.mitigation: specify a ductile low-stress barrier rather than a bright one, apply the embrittlement bake per the published standard class soon after plating, keep the topcoat until after forming, and refuse the work if the shop cannot bake

edge_cases.description: A zinc die-cast casting bleeds entrapped solution and blisters days after an apparently perfect finish
edge_cases.trigger: porous costume casting completed and delivered without a sealing strategy
edge_cases.mitigation: protective alkaline strike plus a sealing copper build on this substrate class, longer drain and dry before the finish, and an honest not-plateable escalation to intake when the casting is too porous to carry a stack

edge_cases.description: A nickel-plated batch is stranded overnight by a rectifier fault before its gold layer
edge_cases.trigger: an unplanned hold between the barrier and the gold tank
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the surface as passive: reactivate or re-strike per the written interface rule before the gold, record the hold in the job record, and bend-test a coupon from the batch before release

edge_cases.description: A customer insists on the cheapest flash gold on a ring shank they intend to wear daily
edge_cases.trigger: a wear-class mismatch requested by name and by price
edge_cases.mitigation: quote the class the wear demands, offer the flash only with the wear expectation disclosed in writing, and never let a heavier barrier be described as compensating for gold the shank will rub through

edge_cases.description: A finished flash job reads pale and washed out rather than warm gold
edge_cases.trigger: very thin gold over a bright white barrier lets the underlayer colour read through
edge_cases.mitigation: increase the gold band to cover read-through rather than tinting a coating or blaming the gold bath, and re-quote the job if the customer wants the warmer hue

edge_cases.description: A trade account asks for a nickel-free label on goods whose only protection is a clear coating over a nickel stack
edge_cases.trigger: a customer-side label requirement that the stack cannot support
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the label in writing, explain that release is assessed after simulated wear and corrosion, offer a nickel-free stack as the compliant alternative, and escalate the claim question to the compliance specialist

edge_cases.description: Thickness measurement cannot resolve the underplate or reads through a small, curved feature
edge_cases.trigger: a geometry or a layer thinness outside what the measurement method can honestly report
edge_cases.mitigation: measure a flat witness coupon run in the same rack position, escalate to a sectioned referee when a number is disputed, and report the method and its limits alongside the value rather than the value alone

edge_cases.description: Stainless work passes a tape test on the bench and peels at the wrap test the next day
edge_cases.trigger: the passive film reformed between the strike and the next layer, or the strike was entered without current
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm live entry, remove the rinse delay after the strike, re-run a coupon through the corrected sequence and bend-test it before any customer work follows

edge_cases.description: A single mixed-metal piece contains brass, a silver solder seam and a stainless spring in one assembly
edge_cases.trigger: an assembly whose components demand different first layers
edge_cases.mitigation: design to the most demanding component, warn that the other components may finish differently, consider selective or brush work for the mismatched part, and escalate to intake when no single stack serves the assembly acceptably

edge_cases.description: A supplier reformulates a purchased barrier system between two runs of the same repeat order
edge_cases.trigger: a data-sheet or composition change on a proprietary nickel-free or barrier system
edge_cases.mitigation: re-read the declaration for nickel content and window changes, re-qualify the stack on a coupon before customer work, and update the recorded stack and any compliance claim that relied on the old declaration

workflow.action: Capture the stack brief for this specific piece
workflow.description: Record substrate and its evidence, wear and skin-contact answers, any post-plate forming or sizing plan, the market of sale and the wording the seller intends to use
workflow.artifact: written stack brief for the job
workflow.gate: every input is present and the intended claim is stated before any layer is chosen

workflow.action: Fork the design on the verified substrate class
workflow.description: Route the job to the brass, silver, mild steel, stainless, zinc die-cast or previously-plated branch on verified identity, flagging mixed-metal components
workflow.artifact: substrate routing decision with the constraining component named
workflow.gate: the substrate class rests on test evidence rather than appearance, and mixed-metal pieces carry the component that governs the stack

workflow.action: Take the nickel decision before any barrier is chosen
workflow.description: For skin-contact goods, decide nickel-bearing with planned testing or nickel-free by design, and record the jurisdiction rule consulted with its date
workflow.artifact: dated nickel decision in the job record
workflow.gate: the decision is explicit, covers strike and gold alloy as well as the barrier, and names the rule checked for the market of sale

workflow.action: Test the candidate route against the shop's safety capability
workflow.description: Confirm every chemistry the stack calls for can be stored, segregated, ventilated and run by trained staff, and substitute a purchased alternative or route the job out where it cannot
workflow.artifact: tank route with its hazard and segregation obligations listed
workflow.gate: no cyanide-bearing and acid chemistry share storage, drainage or an unsegregated sequence, and every bath in the route exists in-house under its obligation class

workflow.action: Set the wear class and the gold architecture
workflow.description: Fix the gold roles — strike, build, colour — and the class band from the piece's hardest-worn zone, checking any hard-gold hardener against the nickel decision
workflow.artifact: gold layer specification with target bands
workflow.gate: the gold class matches the wear class and the wear expectation that will be disclosed, and no hardener contradicts the nickel decision

workflow.action: Choose the barrier system and the layer combination
workflow.description: Select nickel variant, nickel-free class or copper-plus-barrier duplex so that diffusion blocking, levelling and ductility duties are each carried by a named layer
workflow.artifact: barrier and duplex specification with the property each layer buys
workflow.gate: every layer names a property a simpler stack would not deliver, and the ductility requirement of any post-plate forming is satisfied

workflow.action: Allocate the thickness budget across the stack
workflow.description: Give the barrier its minimum for substrate and wear class first, then the gold, and record what gave way if the budget did not reach
workflow.artifact: per-layer target thickness table with verification methods
workflow.gate: every layer has a target band and a named verification method, and any reduction shows the class and claim changed rather than the barrier

workflow.action: Specify the strike and the rules for every interface
workflow.description: Write the entry rule, wet-transfer requirement, maximum hold and reactivation step for each interface, including live entry where the chemistry demands it
workflow.artifact: layer sequence annotated with entry rules and hold limits
workflow.gate: every interface carries an entry rule and a hold limit, and the reactivation path for held work is written down

workflow.action: Check chemical adjacency across the sequence
workflow.description: Confirm no layer feeds a bath it would poison and that every transition names what it must not carry forward, inserting a separation step where needed
workflow.gate: each transition states what it must not carry forward and no incompatible or unsafe adjacency remains in the route

workflow.action: Build the stack and verify it against the specification
workflow.description: Run the sequence with a witness coupon in the rack, then measure thickness and test adhesion by the planned method classes
workflow.artifact: measured stack results with method and coupon reference
workflow.gate: measured values exist for the layers that carry a claim, adhesion passes its test class, and no calculated figure is recorded as a measured one

workflow.action: Decide and apply the topcoat route last
workflow.description: Choose molecular, wax, electrophoretic, sol-gel or lacquer class, or none, on the finished formed piece
workflow.artifact: topcoat decision with class and reason
workflow.gate: the piece is fully formed and finished before coating, and no compliance or thickness claim rests on the coating

workflow.action: Close the as-built record and settle the claim
workflow.description: Write the substrate, every layer with target and measured value, verification method, nickel decision, topcoat route and the exact wording the shop will stand behind
workflow.artifact: as-built stack record with the agreed claim wording
workflow.gate: every field is present and any claim the record cannot support is refused in writing and escalated rather than softened

dominance_rules.rule: Skin-contact nickel-release compliance dominates barrier cost, availability and convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: an article that breaches a skin-contact restriction cannot be sold or worn, and the layer cannot be removed later without destroying the whole stack
dominance_rules.trigger: any stack decision on a piece in prolonged skin contact where nickel is the cheap or convenient option
dominance_rules.action: specify a nickel-free stack or plan release testing, record the dated jurisdiction check, and quote the cost difference rather than absorbing it by reinstating nickel

dominance_rules.rule: Safety and segregation obligations dominate schedule, throughput and job value
dominance_rules.rationale: cyanide-bearing chemistry meeting acid is a fatal-gas event, not a quality problem, and no order is worth it
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed stack requires chemistry the shop cannot store, segregate, ventilate or staff, or a deadline invites a shortcut across the segregation line
dominance_rules.action: redesign the stack around a purchased alternative or route the job to a shop that can run it safely; never co-store, co-drain or sequence the incompatible chemistries together

dominance_rules.rationale: a passivated or dried interface produces delayed peeling that surfaces on the customer rather than on the bench, so the saved hour costs a whole rebuild
dominance_rules.trigger: a half-built stack has waited past its hold limit or a live-entry step is inconvenient to set up
dominance_rules.action: reactivate or re-strike before the next layer and log the hold, or strip and restart; never plate onto a surface that has gone passive

dominance_rules.rule: The barrier keeps its minimum and the claim gives way when the budget is short
dominance_rules.rationale: the barrier carries diffusion blocking and corrosion life, so cutting it destroys the finish while cutting the claim only costs a conversation
dominance_rules.trigger: money, gold price or tank time will not fund both the barrier minimum and the gold band the claimed class requires
dominance_rules.action: hold the barrier, reduce the gold class, and disclose the revised wear expectation and claim to the customer before running

dominance_rules.rule: Measurement dominates calculation and recipe for anything the shop says out loud
dominance_rules.rationale: calculated thickness assumes an efficiency and a current distribution the piece may not have given, and a claim rests on evidence rather than arithmetic
dominance_rules.trigger: a thickness, class or compliance statement is about to leave the shop
dominance_rules.action: quote the measured value with its method, or state the figure explicitly as an estimate and name the method that produced it

dominance_rules.rule: Verified substrate evidence dominates the customer's description and the shop's assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: the substrate fork decides the first layer, and a wrong fork loses the whole run and sometimes the piece
dominance_rules.trigger: the piece's identity rests on appearance, on a hallmark nobody read, or on what the owner believes it is
dominance_rules.action: route the piece back for identification by test-method class before the stack is designed

dominance_rules.rationale: plated goods misdescribed as solid or as more durable than the stack allows destroy the trade book and expose the shop
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer or trade account asks for wording the stack and its record do not support
dominance_rules.action: refuse the wording in writing, offer the stack that would support it with its price, and escalate the claim question rather than negotiating the description

dominance_rules.rule: Irreversibility on customer goods dominates process preference
dominance_rules.rationale: stripping and heavy build with cut-back remove metal from a piece that cannot be replaced
dominance_rules.trigger: the ideal stack requires stripping, aggressive levelling or any other irreversible step on a customer's piece
dominance_rules.action: obtain documented approval with a dated condition record, or build the best stack the current surface allows and disclose the limit

dominance_rules.rule: The supplier's technical data sheet dominates shop habit for every purchased system
dominance_rules.rationale: windows, compatibilities and composition belong to the specific product, and habit carried from another product is how a stack silently goes out of spec
dominance_rules.trigger: a bath is set up, replenished, sequenced or substituted, or a supplier revises the product
dominance_rules.action: work from the current data sheet and declaration for that product, re-qualify on a coupon after any change, and update the recorded stack

dominance_rules.rule: Ductility dominates brightness and levelling wherever the piece will be worked after plating
dominance_rules.rationale: a hard bright underplate cracks at forming and sizing strains and takes the gold with it
dominance_rules.trigger: the piece will be bent, coiled, sized, set or otherwise strained after the stack is built
dominance_rules.action: specify the low-stress ductile barrier, achieve the surface finish before plating, and leave any hard topcoat until after forming

anti_rework_rules.rule: Take the nickel decision before choosing the barrier tank
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a finished skin-contact article whose only route to compliance is stripping and rebuilding the entire stack

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the substrate class before writing the stack
anti_rework_rules.prevents: running a passive metal down the mild-steel route and losing an entire batch to peeling

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the wear class and the disclosed expectation before quoting a gold band
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a flash-class stack sold as durable and returned as a warranty claim the shop cannot defend

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide ductile versus bright barrier before any layer goes on a piece that will be formed or sized
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cracked stack at the bend that can only be fixed by stripping and replating the whole piece

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the levelling strategy before the barrier layer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering under a finished stack that the surface needed levelling, which cannot be added from above

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm every bath the stack calls for exists in-house and in window before the first tank
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a half-built stack stranded mid-sequence while a missing chemistry is ordered, with every interface going passive in the meantime

anti_rework_rules.rule: Plan the verification and put a witness coupon in the rack before the run starts
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a finished job with no measurable surface, where proving the stack means cutting the customer's piece

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check chemical adjacency before committing the tank order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: poisoning the most expensive bath in the shop and the weeks of dull deposits and bath treatment that follow

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply any hard topcoat only after all forming, sizing and setting is complete
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cracked and whitened coating along every bend, which can only be repaired by stripping the coating and recoating

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record each layer as it is built rather than reconstructing the stack at handover
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a dispute the shop cannot answer and a repeat order that cannot be rebuilt to the same specification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a coupon or a returned piece fails an adhesion test at a bend or shows peeling at one interface
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the strike choice and its entry rule, the interface hold times and the ductility of the barrier before changing anything about the gold

iteration_protocol.trigger: spotting, halos or tarnish bloom appear on pieces whose gold thickness measures on target
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as a porosity and underplate problem: revisit barrier thickness and smoothness, then reconsider whether a sealing class is warranted

iteration_protocol.trigger: the market of sale changes, a trade customer begins exporting, or a skin-contact rule is revised
iteration_protocol.action: retake the nickel decision for the affected work, re-plan the barrier route, and update every recorded claim that relied on the old rule check

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured thickness lands outside its target band for a layer or a geometry
iteration_protocol.action: re-allocate the micron budget, hand the delivery question to the electrical-control side of the specialist, and re-measure a coupon before further customer work

iteration_protocol.trigger: flash-class work reads pale or washed out against the retained reference
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as colour read-through from the barrier and increase the gold band rather than tinting a coating or blaming the gold bath

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier revises a purchased barrier, strike or topcoat system, or its composition declaration changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the data sheet and declaration, re-qualify the stack on a coupon before customer work, and update the recorded stack and any claim resting on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: replate work from one source returns more often than new work, or strip decisions keep uncovering surprises
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the replate branch: require a test area, revisit the strip-versus-build criteria and the approval record, and re-price the class if the failure rate persists

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because every layer decision is downstream of what the piece is, how it will be worn, whether nickel is permitted and which chemistries the shop can run safely; the mechanism nodes (diffusion and pore corrosion) come next because they are what the barrier exists to defeat and they set the minimum any stack must satisfy; the layer-class and combination nodes then choose the specific strike, barrier and gold roles and allocate microns across them; the substrate-application nodes apply that design to the hard cases a jewelry bench actually meets; and verification, topcoat and the as-built record come last because they measure, protect and account for a stack that has already been designed correctly, which is the only order in which a failure costs a conversation rather than a rebuild.
